'''Beatriz Susana Cougnet de Roederer''' (16 September 1930 – 12 September 2022) was a pioneer of Argentine physics, specializing in the field of cosmic radiation and high-speed physics.

== Biography ==
Beatriz Cougnet was born in Lausanne, Switzerland, but her parents, Fausto and Susana, were both Argentine citizens<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Beatriz Roederer Obituary (2022) - Boulder, CO - The Daily Camera |url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/dailycamera/name/beatriz-roederer-obituary?id=36521045 |access-date=2023-10-30 |website=Legacy.com}}</ref> so she was raised in Argentina since the age of one. She studied physics and mathematics at the [[University of Buenos Aires]] (UBA) and obtained her M.Sc. degree on 18 December 1952. When the Argentine Atomic Energy Commission was created, Cougnet was one of the first four researchers hired to work on high-energy fundamental particle physics.<ref name=":0" />

Cougnet made important contributions to Argentine science and is considered a pioneer in her field of research, together with [[Estrella Mazzoli de Mathov]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=2011-07-06 |title=Las primeras investigaciones |url=http://www.cienciahoy.org.ar/ln/hoy71/investigaciones.htm |access-date=2023-10-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110706084508/http://www.cienciahoy.org.ar/ln/hoy71/investigaciones.htm |archive-date=2011-07-06 }}</ref> Juana M. Cardoso, Adulio Cichini, Horacio Ghielmetti, [[Emma Pérez Ferreira|Emma V. Pérez Ferreira]], [[Juan Gualterio Roederer|Juan G. Roederer]] and Pedro Waloschek.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-07-17 |title=RAYOS CÓSMICOS EN LA ARGENTINA - Observatorio Pierre Auger |url=https://visitantes.auger.org.ar/index.php/rayos-cosmicos-en-la-argentina/ |access-date=2023-10-30 |language=es-AR}}</ref> She also served as thesis director for a local doctoral student researching nuclear reactions recorded at the [[Bevatron]] particle accelerator in [[Berkeley, California|Berkeley]], California.<ref name=":0" /> 

Cougnet conducted research on cosmic radiation at the Nuclear Plates Laboratory of the [[National Atomic Energy Commission]] (CNEA) in Argentina, around 1950, laying the groundwork for the founding of the National Center for Cosmic Radiation (now called the Institute of Astronomy and Space Physics, IAFE) at the University of Buenos Aires in 1960. At the end of 1949, Cougnet went to Germany and visited the laboratory of [[Werner Heisenberg]] at the [[Max Planck Society|Max Planck Institute]] in [[Göttingen]] where she learned about the work with nuclear emulsions directed by Martin Teucher. In 1950–1951, Cougnet and Juan Roederer, still students, exposed nuclear plates with photographic emulsions at high altitudes in the [[Andes|Andes mountains]] of Argentina. In that way, they obtained the second reported detection of [[Subatomic particle|subatomic particles]] called ''pi [[Meson|mesons]],'' or [[Pion|''pions'']]. In early 1953, Cougnet and Roederer undertook the last expedition to expose emulsions at higher geomagnetic latitudes, on the slopes of the [[Lanín]] volcano near [[Bariloche]], Argentina.<ref name=":1" /> 

In June 1966, the political landscape in Argentina turned dangerous because of the [[coup d'état]], so she and Roederer emigrated to Colorado in the United States with their four children and three surviving parents.<ref name=":0" />

In 1977, Roederer accepted the position of director of the [[Geophysical Institute]] of the [[University of Alaska Fairbanks|University of Alaska]], in [[Fairbanks, Alaska|Fairbanks]], prompting Cougnet, Roederer and a few family members to move again. Later, after living in Alaska for 37 years, Cougnet and Roederer were asked by their children to move back to Colorado.<ref name=":0" />

== Personal life ==
Beatriz was the wife of Juan G. Roederer,<ref>Roederer, Juan. (2019). Space Physics from Both Ends of the Americas, 1949–2019. Journal of Geophysical Research: Space Physics. 124. 10.1029/2019JA027049. </ref> an Italian-born Argentine physicist, whom she met during her high school studies, and with whom she had four children: Ernesto, Irene, Silvia and Mario.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |title=Early Cosmic-Ray Research in Argentina |url=https://pubs.aip.org/physicstoday/article/56/1/32/898844/Early-Cosmic-Ray-Research-in-ArgentinaThe-1950s |access-date=2023-10-30 |journal=Physics Today|date=2003 |doi=10.1063/1.1554134 |last1=Roederer |first1=Juan G. |volume=56 |issue=1 |pages=32–37 |bibcode=2003PhT....56a..32R |url-access=subscription }}</ref> After their third child was born in 1958, she left research and devoted herself to family care. She died in Boulder, Colorado at the age of 91 in 2022.<ref name=":0" />
